ca_hager_boulder.blurb: Hager Boulder is a single block on the hillside above the Iron Man Boulder, in Buttermilk Country outside Bishop on the Eastern Sierra, at about 6,400 feet. It is a small granodiorite bouldering stop with eight problems, nearly all of them around V0, plus one V4 face that stands well apart from the rest. The block makes an easy detour from the neighbouring Iron Man problems for climbers who want a few low-grade lines or a single harder project during a day at the Buttermilks.
ca_hager_boulder.approach: From the west lot, wander up and to the right toward the Iron Man Boulder, then continue a short distance further up the hillside (about 30 yards) to reach the block.

ca_manx_boulders_southeast_face.blurb: This is one face of the Manx Boulders in Joshua Tree National Park, set behind Cyclops Rock a short walk from the Hidden Valley area. It has eight problems on monzogranite, running from V-easy up to about V3, with most of them in the V0 to V2 range. The problems here see less traffic than those on the opposite face of the same boulder pair, and the holds feel less slick. It suits a warm-up session or an easy circuit close to the campground.
ca_manx_boulders_southeast_face.approach: Follow the trail from the Hidden Valley area past the end of Cyclops Rock and around to its back side, where the boulders stand by themselves. The walk takes roughly 5 to 10 minutes.

ca_main_buttress.blurb: Main Buttress is the principal wall of Deadman Buttress at Chipmunk Flat, beside the Sonora Pass Highway (108) at roughly 9,200 feet. Faces rise four to five pitches, with comfortable belay ledges, and nearly every route can be descended by rappel. A bold arete forms the left edge, while the section to its right holds steadier, higher-quality lines. There are eight routes, six trad and two sport, mostly around 5.10 with a couple of 5.11s, one 5.9 and a single 5.4. Pitches can be combined into longer outings.

ca_left_side_boulder_reach_for_it.blurb: This slabby boulder is the downhill half of the Six Gun pair, in the Lone Valley Boulders near Susanville in northeast California, at about 5,600 feet. It is only about 50 yards from the road. Eight problems cover the range from VB through V2, with most at V0 or easier and two at V2, which makes it a suitable first stop for newer boulderers. The steeper, taller half of the pair sits alongside it.

ca_dog_house_ledge.blurb: Dog House Ledge is a bolted wall tucked into the Monkeyface Falls canyon along the Highway 38 crags in the San Bernardino Mountains, at around 4,800 feet. It has eight sport routes. Half sit in the 5.11 range, with the rest between 5.6 and 5.8. The wall faces west and stays shaded until about 2 PM, then picks up sun into the evening, so it works on hot days. Getting in means scrambling a class 4 slope on the right side of the alcove and then using a fixed chain, so bring a harness, a rope and rappel gear.

_expect.name: North Horror Rock - South & East Faces

ca_north_horror_rock_south_east_faces.blurb: These faces form the section of North Horror Rock that can be seen from the road and parking area, in the Hall of Horrors near Sheep Pass in Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,300 feet. The monzogranite holds eight routes, five trad and three sport, mixing crack and face climbing. Four are 5.9, one is 5.10, and three reach 5.11. Several routes are short, and the nearby parking makes for a quick session.
ca_north_horror_rock_south_east_faces.approach: A good trail runs from the paved parking area directly to the base of the rock; reaching some of the routes involves a little scrambling.

ca_hetch_hetchy_dome.blurb: Hetch Hetchy Dome is a two-tiered granite dome of roughly 1,800 feet that rises above the Hetch Hetchy reservoir in Yosemite National Park. The routes are long trad climbs; the eight here are mostly 5.10, with one 5.11 and one 5.12, and some big-wall aid lines also exist. The approach follows the reservoir shoreline on a trail of three to five miles. Few parties visit, so expect to find your own way.

ca_hooter_rock.blurb: Hooter Rock is a large brown formation on the entrance side of the Atom Smasher valley, in the Wonderland area of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,200 feet. Its eight routes lean trad, with three sport lines and one top rope, and span 5.7 to 5.11: three at 5.8, three at 5.10 and one at 5.11. The wall faces north and remains shaded, which keeps it cooler than most of its neighbours. Count on a long hike in from the trailhead.
ca_hooter_rock.approach: Hike the North Wonderland trail into the Atom Smasher valley; the formation stands on the right as the valley opens up, a couple hundred metres off the path.

_conflicts.ca_main_buttress: Stored rock is andesite, but the fetched pages describe the Chipmunk Flat cliffs as granite (https://mountainproject.com/area/114424488/chipmunk-flat, https://mountainproject.com/area/122978399/deadman-buttress). Stored value left unchanged.
